chapter: Jazz's place and the band's future
title: Touring Russia: Vladivostok and Khabarovsk
summary: He describes the band's farthest trip to Vladivostok and Khabarovsk before the recording ends abruptly.

story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Where’s the farthest afield that you guys have played? I know you played across the pond as they say.

Well I guess Khabarovsk, which is a 12 hour train ride north of Vladivostok. In other words we flew nine hours from Moscow to Vladivostok by jet, making one stop in Irkutsk, played in Vladivostok where we’ve been three times, we’ve seen the grandparents of, or the parent’s house of the fellow who played in “The King and I” —

Yul Brynner, yeah. Yul Brynner’s parents have a house that’s still there in Vladivostok. They had mining interests. They apparently paved the roads in Vladivostok. Well Khabarovsk is a city of 600,000 north 12 hours by train, and so we had sleeping compartments and Michael Max and I shared a compartment, because we have a very good intellectual relationship apart from the music, and we could look in across the Amur River into China. And we played in a huge concert hall up there. Now if I can move, I want to show you what they do in Russia. I’m going to give you these. I forgot to give them to you before but let me just bring this up. This has never happened in America.
